As {{BuildR2Cite|26|Droid Directory}} establishes that R5-J2 is an R5 unit, it must have shared those characteristics. |line=[[R-series]]''[[Star Wars: The Visual Encyclopedia]]'' |model=Modified [[R5 series astromech droid|R5-series unit]]{{BuildR2Cite|26|Droid Directory}} |class=[[Astromech droid]] |cost= |length= |width= |height=0.97 [[meter]]s |mass= |gender= |pronouns= |sensor=Black |plating=*[[Color|Black]]{{SideshowCite|set=Sixth Scale Figures|pack=R5-J2 Imperial Astromech Droid|link=collectibles/star-wars-r5-j2-imperial-astromech-droid-sideshow-collectibles-100383}} *Copper |armament= |equipment= |affiliation=[[Galactic Empire]]{{Film|VI}} }} {{Quote|Lord Vader, this is an unexpected pleasure. We're honored by your presence.|Tiaan Jerjerrod greets Vader on behalf of R5-J2 and the others present|audio=Jerjerrod-Honored-ROTJ.flac|}} '''R5-J2''' was an [[Galactic Empire|Imperial]] modified [[R5 series astromech droid]] stationed on board the [[DS-2 Death Star II Mobile Battle Station|Death Star II]] [[superweapon]] while the [[battle station]] was under construction in the [[Endor system]]. The [[R-series|droid]] was present in one of the [[Death Star]]'s [[hangar]]s for the arrival of the [[Dark Lord of the Sith|Sith Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]] on board the [[Space station|station]] in [[4 ABY]]. R5-J2 was then also present in the hangar for the arrival of [[Galactic Emperor]] [[Darth Sidious|Sheev Palpatine]] shortly before the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]] [[Battle of Endor|attacked]] the Death Star. The [[Astromech droid|astromech]] was still stationed on board the superweapon during the battle, which ended with the station's destruction. ==Biography== R5-J2 was an [[R5 series astromech droid]] manufactured by [[Industrial Automaton]] that served the [[Galactic Empire]] during its [[Galactic Civil War|war]] against the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]]. In [[4 ABY]],''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of {{Film|VI}} to [[4 ABY]]. the [[R-series]] [[astromech droid]] was stationed on board the [[DS-2 Death Star II Mobile Battle Station|Death Star II]] [[superweapon]] while it was under construction above the [[moon]] [[Endor]] in the [[Endor system]]. The [[droid]] stood beside a similar unit near the wall of one of the [[Death Star]]'s [[hangar]]s as part of the group of Imperial personnel led by [[Moff]] [[Tiaan Jerjerrod]] that were present for the arrival of the [[Dark Lord of the Sith|Sith Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]] when he arrived on the [[battle station]] to speed up its construction. [[File:R5-J2-ROTJ.png|thumb|left|300px|R5-J2 (center) was present for the arrival of Darth Vader on the Death Star II.]] R5-J2 also witnessed the momentous arrival of [[Galactic Emperor]] [[Darth Sidious|Sheev Palpatine]] in [[Hangar 272]]{{EncyclopediaCite|Battle Stations of the Empire and the First Order}} on board the Death Star sometime after Vader arrived. The droid stood in a similar position near the wall as to when Vader arrived, but this time in a larger group of droids. The astromech was still stationed on the Death Star when the [[Rebel Alliance Navy|Alliance Fleet]] [[Battle of Endor|attacked]] the [[Space station|station]] shortly after the [[Emperor]]'s arrival and destroyed it, with Palpatine also [[Death|perishing]] during the battle. ==Characteristics== R5-J2 was a modified R5 unit and had primarily sleek [[Color|black]] paneling with some copper sections. The droid had two black [[sensor]]s on its dome and stood 0.97 [[meter]]s tall. ==Behind the scenes== ===Origins=== [[File:R5astromechs_btm.jpg|thumb|right|300px|R5-J2 (right) is often erroneously depicted with the three sensors of a separate droid (left) that also appeared in ''Return of the Jedi''.]] R5-J2 first appeared in the [[1983]] [[original trilogy]] film, [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']]. Both Vader's arrival scene and the Emperor's arrival scene were filmed on Stage 6 at [[Elstree Studios]] between [[February 22]] and [[February 24]], [[1982]].''[[The Making of Return of the Jedi]]'' In [[1997]], footage of Vader's arrival on the second Death Star was reused for the [[Sith Lord]]'s return to the [[Executor-class Star Dreadnought|Star Destroyer]] ''[[Executor]]'' from{{Film|V}} the [[planet]] [[Bespin]] in the [[The Star Wars Trilogy Special Edition|''Special Edition'']] release of the [[1980]] film [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']]. As such, R5-J2 is seen in the ''Special Edition'' version alongside other Imperial personnel from ''Return of the Jedi'', however, this article assumes these to be separate characters. The name R5-J2 was first used in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity, where it originated on an action figure in the ''[[Star Wars: The Saga Collection]]'' line by [[Hasbro]] in [[2006]]. However, this figure combined visual traits{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: The Saga Collection|pack=#058: R5-J2|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/tsc058r5j2.asp}} from two separate [[R5-series astromech droid|R5 units]] that appeared in the [[Death Star II/Legends|Death Star]] [[Hangar/Legends|hangar]] in ''Return of the Jedi'', using the paneling [[Color/Legends|colors]] from a [[Droid/Legends|droid]] with two [[Sensor/Legends|sensors]] on its dome, but giving it the three dome sensors of the other droid. The [[2008]] reference book ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' then identified the droid with two sensors on its dome as [[R5-J2/Legends|R5-J2]].{{CSWECite|3|72|R5-J2}} ===Appearances in the current canon=== {{Quote|Beep beep?''"
"''This stormtrooper requires that you charge up that speeder.''"
"''Beep beep.''"
"''Orders are orders. There. I should inform you that he said the drive unit is malfunctioning so there may be unforeseen consequences to charging it.|R5-J2 and R-3PO's conversation in ''LEGO Star Wars: The Force Awakens''|''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Force Awakens]]''}} [[File:R5-J2-LEGOTFA.png|thumb|left|300px|R5-J2 appeared on board the ''Finalizer'' in ''LEGO Star Wars: The Force Awakens''.]] In the current ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]], the droid's name first appeared in the [[2015]] "Rise Against the Empire" expansion for the non-canon [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Disney Infinity 3.0]]''. However, the purchasable character using the name was depicted as the R5 unit with three sensors on its dome.''[[Disney Infinity 3.0]]'' The droid was then also a purchasable character in the non-canon video game ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Force Awakens]]'', which was released on [[June 28]], [[2016]],{{SW|url=news/calling-all-jedi-masters-and-master-builders-announcing-lego-star-wars-the-force-awakens|text=Calling All Jedi Masters and Master Builders: Announcing ''LEGO Star Wars: The Force Awakens''}} and depicted the droid with two sensors. In the game, the droid is referred to with he/him pronouns and appears in the mission "Chapter 2: Escape from the Finaliser." The chapter is set during the rogue [[First Order stormtrooper|stormtrooper]] [[Finn]] and the [[Resistance pilot]] [[Poe Dameron]]'s [[Escape from the Finalizer|escape]] from the [[First Order]] [[Resurgent-class Star Destroyer|''Resurgent''-class Star Destroyer]] ''[[Finalizer]]'' in [[34 ABY]].''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' The pair find the astromech sat in an uncharged [[speeder]] in the ''Finalizer''{{'s}} hangar and form a plan to use the [[Repulsorcraft|speeder]] to cause a distraction, but are unable to interact with the terminal beside the vehicle without a [[protocol droid]]. After recruiting the [[3PO-series protocol droid]] [[R-3PO]], the pair have the droid interact with the terminal and then instruct R5-J2 to charge the speeder. In [[binary]], the astromech warns them that the speeder's [[Engine|drive unit]] is malfunctioning and so charging it might have unforeseen effects but complies with the order and also turns the speeder to face a group of First Order personnel. With R5-J2 still in the seat, the speeder then boosts forward toward the personnel before crashing into the hangar floor and exploding. Completing the chapter unlocks R5-J2 as a purchasable character. [[File:R5-J2-Sideshow.png|thumb|right|300px|Various action figures depict an erroneous version of R5-J2.]] The first canonical source in the current canon to use the name was a [[Sideshow Collectibles]] figure of R5-J2 released as part of the [[Sideshow Collectibles|Sixth Scale Figures]] line in [[December]] 2016.{{WebCite|url=https://www.jeditemplearchives.com/content/modules.php?name=JReviews&rop=showcontent&id=2781|text=R5-J2 (Imperial Astromech Droid) - 1:6 Scale Figures|author=Harrison, Paul|date=2017-01-02|work=[https://www.jeditemplearchives.com Jedi Temple Archives]|archivedate=20230331055706}} The figure used the same erroneous combination of three dome sensors with the paneling from the two dome sensor droid as the previous Hasbro figure. The [[2017]] reference book ''[[Star Wars: The Visual Encyclopedia]]'' then canonically applied the name to an image of the droid with two sensors on its dome. A [[2019]] [[Bandai]] figure of the droid then once again depicted the droid with the erroneous combination of features.{{BandaiCite|set=Droid Collection|pack=R5-J2|url=https://www.amazon.co.uk/Bandai-Hobby-R5-J2/dp/B07K2M31CB|nolive=1}} ==Appearances== {{Mediacat|imagecat=Images of R5-J2}} *{{Film|VI}} {{1st}} ===Non-canon appearances=== *''[[Disney Infinity 3.0]]'' *''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Force Awakens]]'' {{1stID|R5-J2}} ==Sources== *{{SWE|characters|darthvader|Darth Vader}} {{Video}} *{{HelmetCollectionCite|9|Weapons & Uniforms}} {{Po}} *{{SideshowCite|set=Sixth Scale Figures|pack=R5-J2 Imperial Astromech Droid|link=collectibles/star-wars-r5-j2-imperial-astromech-droid-sideshow-collectibles-100383}} *''[[Star Wars: The Visual Encyclopedia]]'' {{C|First canonical identification}} *{{BuildR2Cite|26|Droid Directory}} {{Po}} *''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary, New Edition]]'' *{{BandaiCite|set=Droid Collection|pack=R5-J2|url=https://www.amazon.co.uk/Bandai-Hobby-R5-J2/dp/B07K2M31CB|nolive=1}} *{{StoryCite|story=Star Tours (episode)|book=Wikipedia:Behind the Attraction|text=''Behind the Attraction''}} {{Mo}} *''[[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi: A Visual Archive]]'' *{{LEGOCite|num=75392|name=Creative Play Droid Builder}} *''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia: The Comprehensive Guide to the Star Wars Galaxy]]'' ===Non-canon sources=== *''[[LEGO Star Wars Character Encyclopedia Updated Edition]]'' ==Notes and references== {{Reflist}} {{Interlang |ja=R5-J2 |pl=R5-J2 }} [[Category:Droids of the Galactic Empire]] [[Category:Droids with unspecified gender programming]] [[Category:Droids with unspecified pronouns]] [[Category:R5-series astromech droids]]
